notes: PIPELINE (from the library spec) Ingestion → Mode Router selects 'Video-to-Video Style Transfer': transform an existing video clip's visual style while preserving its temporal coherence and structural motion → Input Prep (Nano Banana Pro pre-cleans or generates any needed reference/anchor images) → Omni Flash 1.1 executes the mode's native generation/edit call with correctly structured inputs (frameImages / referenceImages / source video as required) → World-Knowledge Consistency Critic (does the result respect physics, scene logic, and the world-knowledge grounding Omni Flash brings beyond raw photorealism?) → Repair via a follow-up Interactions-API turn (conversational edit) rather than a full regeneration when the mode supports it → Deliver at draft (360p) then promote to 1080p/4K once approved → Package.
STAGE 1 — MODE ROUTER + INPUT PREP Mode: Video-to-Video Style Transfer. Wire only the inputs this mode actually consumes — text brief, one anchor image, up to five references, or an existing clip.
STAGE 2 — INPUT PREP (NANO BANANA PRO) Pre-cleans or generates any anchor and reference frames the mode requires.
STAGE 3 — OMNI FLASH 1.1 EXECUTION The mode's native call. The text-only lane uses a prompt-only video-gen node; the reference lane conditions on the anchor; the edit lane consumes the source video.

STAGE 4 — WORLD-KNOWLEDGE CONSISTENCY CRITIC Does the result respect physics, scene logic and the world knowledge Omni Flash brings beyond raw photorealism? Repair via a follow-up edit turn, not a full regeneration.
STAGE 5 — DRAFT THEN PROMOTE Review at draft resolution, then promote the approved cut to delivery.

M-VT0454_Bluetooth_Speaker___Conversatio.pipeline: video-input → reference-image-input → prompt → video-edit → text-gen → video-edit → text-gen → video-edit → text-gen → video-edit → 3× text-gen → video-edit → download

requires.name: Base video — uploaded or previously generated

notes: PIPELINE (from the library spec) Ingestion → Base Generation produces or accepts the starting video → Edit-Request Parser converts each natural-language note ('make the lighting warmer', 'swap the background to a kitchen', 'change the camera to a low angle') into a structured Interactions-API turn → Omni Flash 1.1 applies each edit conversationally, preserving everything not mentioned in that turn → Turn-by-Turn Diff Critic confirms only the requested change occurred (no unintended drift elsewhere in frame) → Repair (re-issue the turn with tighter scoping) on any unintended drift → Final-state Package once the director approves the accumulated edits.
STAGE 1 — BASE STATE Either an uploaded clip of the Bluetooth Speaker or a generated base. Every turn below edits the accumulated state, not the original.
STAGE 2 — EDIT-REQUEST PARSER + SEQUENTIAL TURNS Each natural-language note becomes one scoped Interactions-style turn. Everything not mentioned in a turn must survive that turn untouched.
STAGE 3 — TURN-BY-TURN DIFF CRITIC Confirms only the requested change occurred in each turn — unintended drift anywhere else in frame is the failure this stage exists to catch.
